assignedReviews.card_evidence: A special chest bone called the keel—big flight muscles attach here and flap the wings so the bird can fly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency targets outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement and food gathering. The keel is an internal chest bone, not an outer body part, and the card only addresses flight muscle attachment, not food gathering. It shares the topic of animal body parts and movement but does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
What lets a bird flap its wings so hard?

A special chest bone called the keel—big flight muscles attach here and flap the wings so the bird can fly.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tumutulong sa ibon na kumampay nang malakas?

Isang espesyal na buto sa dibdib na tinatawag na 'keel'—dito nakakabit ang malalakas na kalamnan na nagpapakampay ng mga pakpak.
copy.bis:
Unsay motabang sa langgam nga makapakapay og kusog?

Usa ka espesyal nga buto sa dughan nga gitawag og 'keel'—dinhi nakakabit ang kusgan nga unod nga magpakapay sa mga pako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use the sun, the stars, and Earth's magnetic field as guides on their journey.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how migrating birds navigate using environmental cues. It does not describe animals changing to better suit their environment, nor mimicry or camouflage, so it does not directly support this adaptation competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use the sun, the stars, and Earth's magnetic field as guides on their journey.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun and stars but only as navigation cues for birds. It does not guide students to observe and describe these celestial objects themselves, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How do migrating birds find their way?

They use the sun, the stars, and Earth's magnetic field as guides on their journey.
copy.tl:
Paano nahahanap ng mga lumilipad na ibon ang tamang daan?

Ginagamit nila ang araw, mga bituin, at ang magnetikong larangan ng Mundo bilang gabay sa kanilang paglalakbay.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkaplag sa mga nagbalhin nga langgam sa ilang dalan?

Gigamit nila ang adlaw, ang mga bituon, ug ang magnetikong natad sa Yuta isip giya sa ilang panaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: old feathers fall out and new ones grow in so the bird can keep flying well
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions feathers (an outer body part) and flying, but it does not describe the outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or identify their role to move and gather food. It focuses on the molting process, not on the structure or function of body parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: old feathers fall out and new ones grow in
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes feather replacement, which is a growth/regrowth process, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Molting is not presented as a characteristic of living things; it is a specific bird behavior.

copy.en:
Why do birds lose their feathers sometimes?

It's called molting — old feathers fall out and new ones grow in so the bird can keep flying well.
copy.tl:
Bakit nalalaglag paminsan-minsan ang balahibo ng ibon?

Tinatawag itong molting — nalalaglag ang lumang balahibo at may bagong tutubo para makapaglipad nang maayos ang ibon.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mangahulog usahay ang balhibo sa langgam?

Gitawag kining molting — mangahulog ang daan nga balhibo ug adunay bag-ong motubo aron makalupad gihapon og maayo ang langgam.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there is no complete path for the electricity to flow down to the ground
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a bird is not shocked because there is no complete circuit path. It does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it teach safe measures in handling electricity. The safety idea is only tangentially related.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there is no complete path for the electricity to flow down to the ground
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses an incomplete circuit path but does not involve assembling or drawing a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer, and no such representation is present. It only touches on circuit completeness.

copy.en:
Why doesn't a bird get shocked when sitting on a single wire?

It is safe because there is no complete path for the electricity to flow down to the ground!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi nakukuryente ang ibon na nakadapo sa isang kawad?

Ligtas siya dahil walang kumpletong daanan para dumaloy ang kuryente papunta sa lupa!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang langgam nga nagtungtong sa usa ka kawad dili makuryente?

Luwas siya kay walay kompletong agianan para modagan ang kuryente paingon sa yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both wings make lift from their shape.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses flight and lift, not measuring distance and time with simple equipment. No instructional support for the measurement skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds flap to pull forward, while airplane wings stay fixed and engines push them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pushing and pulling in the context of propulsion, but does not explore or demonstrate ways to make objects move by natural causes or by people. It is about flight mechanics, not the guided exploration of moving objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds flap to pull forward, while airplane wings stay fixed and engines push them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card references pushing and pulling as propulsion mechanisms, but does not demonstrate how pushes and pulls change speed or direction of an object. No guided activity or demonstration of force effects on motion.

copy.en:
Why do birds flap but airplanes don't?

Both wings make lift from their shape. But birds flap to pull forward, while airplane wings stay fixed and engines push them.
copy.tl:
Bakit pumapagaspas ang ibon pero hindi ang eroplano?

Pareho silang gumagawa ng lift sa hugis. Pero pumapagaspas ang ibon para humila, habang naka-fixed ang pakpak ng eroplano at makina ang nagtutulak.
copy.bis:
Nganong mokampay ang langgam pero dili ang eroplano?

Parehas silang naghimo og lift sa porma. Apan mokampay ang langgam aron mobira, samtang fixed ang pako sa eroplano ug makina ang motulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a beautiful gem with a lovely blue-green color
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions the color of turquoise. G5-E-2 requires exploring/collecting different types of rocks and describing similarities/differences in features such as texture, color, and grain crystal size. The card does not support observation, collection, or comparison of rock features; it merely states a single color attribute of one gemstone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a beautiful gem with a lovely blue-green color
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions only the color of turquoise. G3-M-5 asks to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. While color is a physical property, the card does not describe the property in a way that supports the competency's intent (e.g., hardness, shininess, stretchability). It is only a passing mention of color, not a description of physical properties.

copy.en: The birthstone for December is the turquoise, a beautiful gem with a lovely blue-green color!
copy.tl: Ang birthstone para sa Disyembre ay ang turquoise (turkesa), isang magandang bato na asul-berde ang kulay!
copy.bis: Ang birthstone para sa Disyembre kay ang turquoise (turkesa), usa ka nindot nga bato nga asul-berde og kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This adds to the warming of the atmosphere and the melting of ice.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a mechanism (soot absorbing heat) that contributes to warming and mentions melting ice, but it does not present or identify evidence of global warming/climate change (e.g., temperature records, glacier retreat, sea-level rise). It is a cause-effect statement, not an evidence-identification task.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Black carbon soot in the air absorbs the sun's heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of greenhouse gases in enhanced global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a warming agent (black carbon soot), but soot is not a greenhouse gas. The competency specifically addresses the role of greenhouse gases in enhanced global warming. The card does not mention greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, etc.) or their role, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
How does black carbon soot in the air affect our planet?

Black carbon soot in the air absorbs the sun's heat! This adds to the warming of the atmosphere and the melting of ice.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakaapekto ang black carbon soot sa hangin sa ating planeta?

Ang black carbon soot sa hangin ay sumisipsip ng init ng araw! Nakakadagdag ito sa pag-init ng atmospera at pagkatunaw ng yelo.
copy.bis:
Unsay epekto sa black carbon soot sa hangin sa atong kalibotan?

Ang black carbon soot sa hangin mosuyop sa init sa adlaw! Makadugang kini sa pag-init sa atmospera ug pagtunaw sa yelo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The biggest stars can collapse into a black hole — a place with gravity so strong that not even light can escape!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes black holes formed from collapsing stars, which are not part of the solar system's major celestial objects (Sun, planets, moons, etc.) nor their features or composition. It does not support describing the general structure of the solar system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The biggest stars can collapse into a black hole — a place with gravity so strong that not even light can escape!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars but focuses on black holes, which are not natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime or nighttime. It does not support observing and describing the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars as visible celestial objects.

copy.en: The biggest stars can collapse into a black hole — a place with gravity so strong that not even light can escape!
copy.tl: Ang pinakamalalaking bituin ay maaaring gumuho at maging black hole — isang lugar na napakalakas ng grabidad na kahit liwanag ay hindi makakatakas!
copy.bis: Ang pinakadagko nga mga bituon mahimong mokuyog ug mahimong black hole — usa ka dapit nga kusog kaayo ang grabidad nga bisan ang kahayag dili makaikyas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: space has no air for sound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on exploring and describing how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations (e.g., ringing bell, hearing noises). This card discusses sound transfer in the context of space and black holes, not everyday situations. It touches on the idea that sound needs a medium, but does not directly support the everyday exploration described in the competency.

copy.en:
Is space around a black hole completely silent?

Usually yes, because space has no air for sound! But in thick gas clouds, scientists detected a very low rumble too deep for humans to hear.
copy.tl:
Tahimik ba talaga ang paligid ng black hole sa kalawakan?

Kadalasan oo, dahil walang hangin sa kalawakan para sa tunog! Pero sa makakapal na ulap ng gas, may natuklasan ang mga siyentista na napakababang ugong na hindi naririnig ng tao.
copy.bis:
Hilom ba gyud ang palibot sa black hole sa kawanangan?

Kasagaran oo, tungod kay walay hangin sa kawanangan para sa tingog! Apan sa baga nga panganod sa gas, may nakit-an ang mga siyentista nga ubos kaayong dahunog nga dili madungog sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA programs and observatories teach about stars and space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions astronomy, stars, and space, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features and composition. It only relates to the broad topic of astronomy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA programs and observatories teach about stars and space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars and space but does not involve guided activities to observe and describe natural objects in the sky such as the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. It is only topically related to celestial objects.

copy.en:
How can Filipino kids learn about black holes?

Through astronomy! PAGASA programs and observatories teach about stars and space—even without a black hole in our backyard.
copy.tl:
Paano matututo ang mga batang Pilipino tungkol sa black holes?

Sa pamamagitan ng astronomiya! Ang mga programa ng PAGASA at mga obserbatoryo ay nagtuturo tungkol sa mga bituin at kalawakan.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkat-on sa mga batang Pilipino bahin sa black holes?

Pinaagi sa astronomiya! Ang mga programa sa PAGASA ug mga obserbatoryo nagtudlo bahin sa mga bituon ug kawanangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Do all black holes have the same size?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses black holes and their varying masses, which are not part of the solar system. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system and identifying major celestial objects, their features, and composition. Black holes are extragalactic objects and are not covered by this competency.

copy.en:
Do all black holes have the same size?

No! Some weigh just a few times more than a star, while others at galaxy centers weigh as much as millions or billions of Suns!
copy.tl:
Pare-pareho ba ang laki ng lahat ng black hole?

Hindi! Ang iba ay kasimbigat lang ng ilang bituin, pero ang nasa sentro ng galaksiya ay kasimbigat ng milyon-milyon o bilyon-bilyong Araw!
copy.bis:
Parehas ba ang gidak-on sa tanang black hole?

Dili! Ang uban sama ra og gibug-aton sa pipila ka bituon, samtang ang nasa sentro sa galaksiya sama og gibug-aton sa minilyon o binilyon nga Adlaw!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses light absorption and reflection by black/white objects, but the competency requires guided investigations describing reflection using plane/curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card does not address mirrors, refraction, or the required investigation.

copy.en: A black object absorbs all colors of light so it heats up more, while a white object reflects almost all the light!
copy.tl: Sinisipsip ng itim na bagay ang lahat ng kulay ng liwanag kaya mas umiinit ito, samantalang sinasalamin ng puti ang halos lahat ng liwanag!
copy.bis: Ang itom nga butang nagsuyop sa tanang kolor sa kahayag mao nga mas moinit kini, samtang ang puti nagbalik sa halos tanang kahayag!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions convex mirrors as an everyday application but does not describe or illustrate reflection of light using curved mirrors, nor involve any guided investigation. It only names a use, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: convex mirrors are installed! They give drivers a wider view around corners to avoid collisions.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a use of light-related mirrors but does not explore or describe sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, or engage in guided science activities. It is only a related everyday example.

copy.en: At many narrow street corners and garages in the Philippines, convex mirrors are installed! They give drivers a wider view around corners to avoid collisions.
copy.tl: Sa maraming makitid na kanto at garahe sa Pilipinas, may mga convex mirror! Nagbibigay ito ng mas malawak na tanawin sa mga driver para maiwasan ang banggaan.
copy.bis: Sa daghang makitid nga sulok sa karsada ug garahe sa Pilipinas, naay mga convex mirror! Nagahatag kini og mas halapad nga tanawin sa mga drayber aron malikayan ang mga banggaan.

Tiny markers called antigens on the surface of your red blood cells decide your blood type.

Ang gagmayng mga marka nga gitawag og antigen sa ibabaw sa pula nga selula sa dugo maoy nagbutang sa klase sa imong dugo.

Ang gagmay nga marka nga gitawag og antigen sa ibabaw sa imong pula nga selula sa dugo — kana ang nagtino sa imong klase sa dugo!

Big blue stars are the hottest but burn their fuel fast, so they live short lives. Small red stars burn slowly and last a very long time!

Ang malalaking asul na bituin ang pinakamainit pero mabilis maubos ang gatong kaya maikli ang buhay. Ang maliliit na pula ay dahan-dahan at napakatagal!

Ngano paspas mamatay ang dagko ug asul nga mga bituon?

Ang dagko ug asul nga mga bituon mao ang pinakainit apan paspas mahurot ang gatong kay mubo ang kinabuhi. Ang gagmayng pula hinay molungtad og taas kaayo!

Ang blue whale! Kasinglaki ng maliit na kotse ang puso nito!

Unsang hayop ang adunay pinakadakong kasingkasing?

Ang blue whale! Sama kadako sa gamay nga awto ang kasingkasing niini!

What is the biggest animal ever to live?

The blue whale is the largest animal ever to live on Earth, bigger than any dinosaur — it can grow to about 30 meters long!

Ang blue whale ang pinakamalaking hayop na nabuhay sa Earth, mas malaki pa sa kahit anong dinosaur — umaabot ito ng mga 30 metro ang haba!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga hayop nga nabuhi?

Ang blue whale mao ang pinakadako nga hayop nga nabuhi sa Earth, mas dako pa kaysa bisan unsang dinosaur — makaabot kini og mga 30 ka metro ang gitas-on!

How long is a blue whale?

A blue whale can grow about 30 meters long — as long as three school buses lined up!

Gaano kahaba ang blue whale?

Umaabot ng halos 30 metro ang haba ng blue whale — kasinghaba ng tatlong school bus na magkakasunod!
copy.bis:
Unsa kataas ang blue whale?

Makaabot ug mga 30 ka metro ang gitas-on sa blue whale — sama kataas sa tulo ka school bus nga magkasunod!

What is the loudest animal on Earth?

The blue whale is one of the loudest animals alive, with calls that can reach about 188 decibels!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalakas na hayop sa mundo?

Ang blue whale ay isa sa pinakamalakas na hayop, umaabot ng halos 188 decibels ang tawag nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinaka-saba nga mananap sa kalibotan?

Ang blue whale usa sa pinakasaba nga hayop, moabot ug mga 188 ka decibels ang iyang tawag!

Are paddles only used on the bangka?

Nope! A canoe uses a single-blade paddle. A kayak uses a paddle with a blade on each end, so you can stroke right then left without changing your grip!

Sa bangka lang ginagamit ang sagwan?

Hindi! Ang canoe ay sinasagwan ng sagwan na may isang blade. Ang kayak naman ay may blade sa magkabilang dulo, kaya pwede kang sumagwan sa kanan at kaliwa nang hindi pinapalitan ang hawak!
copy.bis:
Sa bangka lang gamiton ang bugsay?

Dili! Ang canoe gibugsay ug bugsay nga usa ka blade. Ang kayak adunay blade sa duha ka tumoy, busa makahatak ka sa tuo unya sa wala nga dili usbon ang kupot!

copy.en: On a dragon boat, everyone must stroke together! When in sync, pushes add up, making the boat faster and straighter. Uneven timing makes efforts cancel out and the boat wobbles.
copy.tl: Sa dragon boat, kailangang sabay-sabay humatak ang lahat! Kapag sabay, nagdaragdag ang tulak kaya mas mabilis at tuwid ang bangka. Kung magkakanya-kanya, nagkakanselahin ang lakas at gumagewang ang bangka.
copy.bis: Sa dragon boat, kinahanglan dungan ang tanan! Kon dungan, magdugang ang tulak busa mas paspas ug tul-id ang bangka. Kon dili patas, magkansilahay ang kusog ug mag-uyog ang bangka.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying

copy.en: A paddle has three parts: the wide blade that catches water, the long shaft you hold, and the grip at the top. The wide blade matters most—it pushes more water!
copy.tl: Ang sagwan ay may tatlong bahagi: ang malapad na blade na sumasalo sa tubig, ang mahabang shaft na hawak, at ang grip sa itaas. Ang malapad na blade ang pinakamahalaga—mas maraming tubig ang naitutulak nito!
copy.bis: Ang bugsay naay tulo ka bahin: ang lapad nga blade nga modakop sa tubig, ang taas nga shaft nga kuptanan, ug ang grip sa ibabaw. Ang lapad nga blade mao ang labing importante—daghan ang tubig nga matulak niini!

assignedReviews.reason: The card names types of bodies of water but does not identify local examples nor describe how they influence living and non-living components, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What are bodies of water, and why are some salty?

Places like oceans, lakes, rivers, and streams; most water is salty in oceans and fresh in lakes and rivers!
copy.tl:
Ano ang bodies of water, at bakit may mga alat?

Mga lugar gaya ng oceans, lakes, rivers, at streams; karamihan ay alat sa oceans at fresh sa lakes at rivers!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang bodies of water, ug nganong naay mga parat?

Mga dapit sama sa oceans, lakes, rivers, ug streams; kadaghanan parat sa oceans ug fresh sa lakes ug rivers!

Unsa ang normal nga temperatura sa lawas sa tawo?

Ang normal nga temperatura sa lawas sa tawo kay mga 37 degrees Celsius, o 37°C!

copy.tl: Ang normal na temperatura ng iyong katawan ay mga 37 degrees Celsius (37°C). Ito ang tamang init para maging malusog at maganda ang pakiramdam mo!
copy.bis: Ang normal nga temperatura sa imong lawas mga 37 degrees Celsius (37°C). Kini mao ang sakto nga kainit aron mahimsog ug nindot ang imong gibati!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)

copy.en:
What is normal human body temperature?

Normal human body temperature is about 37°C — if it rises much higher, the person has a fever and may need care.
copy.tl:
Ano ang normal na temperatura ng katawan ng tao?

Ang normal na temperatura ng katawan ng tao ay mga 37°C — kapag tumaas nang malaki, may lagnat ang tao at baka kailanganin ng pag-aalaga.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang normal nga temperatura sa lawas sa tawo?

Ang normal nga temperatura sa lawas sa tawo mga 37°C — kung motaas og dako, adunay lagnat ang tawo ug tingali kinahanglan og pag-atiman.

copy.en: About three-quarters of your brain is water — that's why not drinking enough can affect your thinking and focus.
copy.tl: Halos tatlong-kapat ng iyong utak ay tubig — kaya nakaka-apekto sa pag-iisip at konsentrasyon kapag kulang ka sa tubig.
copy.bis: Mga tulo-ka-upat sa imong utok tubig — mao nga makaapekto sa imong panghunahuna ug konsentrasyon kon kulang ka og tubig.

copy.en: It's important that the water you drink is clean and safe — dirty water can carry germs and make you sick!
copy.tl: Mahalagang malinis at ligtas ang iniinom mong tubig — ang maruming tubig ay maaaring magdala ng bakterya at magdulot ng sakit!
copy.bis: Importante nga limpyo ug luwas ang imong giinom nga tubig — ang hugaw nga tubig makadala og bakterya ug makasakit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's why water is so important for life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that water is important for life but does not identify water as one of the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It focuses on the body's water percentage, not on the need itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's why water is so important for life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water's importance for life but does not specifically recognize water as a basic need of plants and animals. It is about human body composition, not plant/animal needs.

copy.en:
How much of your body is water?

More than half of your body is water — about 60 percent in a child. That's why water is so important for life.
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming tubig ang laman ng katawan mo?

Mahigit kalahati ng iyong katawan ay tubig — humigit-kumulang 60 porsyento sa isang bata. Kaya napakahalaga ng tubig para mabuhay.
copy.bis:
Pila ka porsyento sa imong lawas ang tubig?

Kapin sa katunga sa imong lawas kay tubig — mga 60 porsyento sa usa ka bata. Mao nga importante kaayo ang tubig aron mabuhi.

assignedReviews.reason: Names seeds and underground pods; does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation as reproductive methods.

copy.en: Peanuts are the seeds of a legume plant that's unusual — its pods grow underground! They're also rich in protein that helps build your body.
copy.tl: Ang mani ay binhi ng halamang-gisantes na kakaiba dahil sa ilalim ng lupa tumutubo ang bunga nito! Mayaman din ito sa protina na nagpapalakas sa katawan.
copy.bis: Ang mani binhi sa tanom nga legume nga talagsaon kay sa ilawom sa yuta motubo ang bunga niini! Dato usab kini sa protina nga makapalig-on sa lawas.

copy.bis: Kon mas daghan ang bonds tali sa duha ka atoms, mas mubo ug mas kusgan ang bond, busa ang triple bonds ang pinakamubo ug pinakakusgan.

copy.en: Bonding explains why atoms combine in fixed amounts! In water, it's always two hydrogen to one oxygen because each atom seeks a stable number of electrons.
copy.tl: Ipinapaliwanag ng bonding kung bakit nagsasama ang mga atoms sa tiyak na dami! Sa tubig, laging dalawang hydrogen sa isang oxygen dahil naghahanap ang bawat atom ng matatag na bilang ng electrons.
copy.bis: Ang bonding nagpasabot ngano nga ang mga atoms magtipon sa tino nga gidaghanon! Sa tubig, kanunayng duha ka hydrogen sa usa ka oxygen kay ang matag atom mangita og lig-on nga gidaghanon sa electrons.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses bone strength and osteoporosis prevention through exercise, but it does not describe how the skeletal system works, which is the focus of G4-L-1. It shares the topic of bones but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Running and jumping while young help build strong, dense bones — and strong bones now protect against osteoporosis later in life.
copy.tl: Ang pagtakbo at paglukso habang bata pa ay tumutulong magpatibay ng buto — at ang matibay na buto ngayon ay proteksyon laban sa osteoporosis balang araw.
copy.bis: Ang pagdagan ug paglukso samtang bata pa motabang magpatig-a sa buto — ug ang lig-on nga buto karon proteksyon batok sa osteoporosis sa umaabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Red bone marrow inside your bones makes red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Where blood cells are made (marrow) is origin, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Red bone marrow inside your bones makes red blood cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Marrow making blood is not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory as a set.

copy.en:
Where does the body make blood?

Red bone marrow inside your bones makes red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets that your body needs!
copy.tl:
Saan ginagawa ang dugo sa katawan?

Ang pulang bone marrow sa loob ng iyong mga buto ang gumagawa ng red blood cell, white blood cell, at platelet na kailangan ng katawan!
copy.bis:
Asa gibuhat ang dugo sa lawas?

Ang pulang bone marrow sa sulod sa imong mga bukog ang nagbuhat sa red blood cell, white blood cell, ug platelet nga gikinahanglan sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Red blood cells are made inside our bones, in a part called the bone marrow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Where red blood cells are made is origin, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made inside our bones, in a part called the bone marrow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Marrow making blood is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
Where are red blood cells made?

Red blood cells are made inside our bones, in a part called the bone marrow.
copy.tl:
Saan ginagawa ang pulang selula ng dugo?

Ang mga pulang selula ng dugo ay ginagawa sa loob ng buto, sa bahaging tinatawag na utak ng buto (bone marrow).
copy.bis:
Asa gihimo ang pula nga selula sa dugo?

Ang pula nga selula sa dugo gihimo sulod sa bukog, sa bahin nga gitawag og kinauyokan sa bukog (bone marrow).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: So it can support your body! But inside, soft marrow makes new blood cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Hard bone plus marrow is skeletal, not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory as a set.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: soft marrow makes new blood cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Marrow making blood is origin, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
Why is bone hard outside, soft inside?

So it can support your body! But inside, soft marrow makes new blood cells.
copy.tl:
Bakit matigas sa labas ang buto?

Para masuportahan ang katawan mo! Pero sa loob, may malambot na marrow na gumagawa ng bagong dugo.
copy.bis:
Ngano gahi sa gawas ang bukog?

Aron masuportahan ang imong lawas! Apan sa sulod, adunay humok nga marrow nga naghimo og bag-ong dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: how our bones protect us
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bones, rib cage, and skull as inspiration for protective engineering, but it does not describe how the skeletal system works. It only references bones as a protective frame, which is related vocabulary but does not directly support the competency of describing how the skeletal system functions.

copy.en: Engineers borrow ideas from how our bones protect us. Sturdy helmets and the 'roll cage' inside a race car work like a copied rib cage or skull — a strong frame outside guarding what matters inside.
copy.tl: Kumukuha ng ideya ang mga inhinyero mula sa paraan ng pagprotekta ng ating buto. Ang matitibay na helmet at ang 'roll cage' ng kotse-karera ay parang gayang gusok o bungo — matibay na balangkas sa labas na nag-iingat ng mahalaga sa loob.
copy.bis: Ang mga inhinyero mokuha og ideya gikan sa paagi sa pagpanalipod sa atong bukog. Ang lig-on nga helmet ug ang 'roll cage' sa sulod sa race car sama sa gisundog nga gusok o bungo — lig-on nga bayanan sa gawas nga nanalipod sa importante sa sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even in a transverse wave, particles move across this arrow, but the wave still travels forward.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of transverse waves (particles move perpendicular to travel direction) but does not mention longitudinal waves or compare the two types. It provides background knowledge about transverse waves but does not directly support identifying differences and similarities between longitudinal and transverse waves.

copy.en: Every wave has a clear travel direction you can point to! Even in a transverse wave, particles move across this arrow, but the wave still travels forward.
copy.tl: Bawat alon ay may direksyon na pwede mong ituro! Kahit ang mga particle sa transverse wave ay gumagalaw patawid, tuloy pa rin ang paglalakbay ng alon.
copy.bis: Ang matag balod naay direksyon nga pwede nimo ituro! Bisan pa nga ang mga particle sa transverse wave molihok tabok, nagpadayon gihapon ang pagbiyahe sa balod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: building the nest and feeding the chicks until the babies can fly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes parental care in birds, not the stages of a bird's life cycle (egg, chick, adult) or a comparison of life cycles across mammals, birds, and plants. It shares the bird topic but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: feeding the chicks until the babies can fly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions chicks growing until they can fly, which hints at growth, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a concept. It is about parental behavior, not the general characteristics of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: both parents pitch in — building the nest and feeding the chicks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows parents caring for chicks, which is an example of living things depending on each other, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs. It lacks the explanatory component and broader environmental context.

copy.en: In many bird families, both parents pitch in — building the nest and feeding the chicks until the babies can fly!
copy.tl: Sa maraming ibon, magkasama ang mga magulang — gumagawa ng pugad at nagpapakain sa mga sisiw hanggang sa makalipad na ang mga ito!
copy.bis: Sa daghang langgam, managsama ang ginikanan — naghimo sa salag ug nagpakaon sa mga piso hangtod nga makalupad na ang mga bata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Just be careful of its sharp thorns, which can scratch your skin.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions thorns but only warns about their sharpness causing scratches; it does not describe the purpose of thorns as a specialized plant structure (e.g., defense).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Just be careful of its sharp thorns, which can scratch your skin.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that thorns can harm humans, which is an interaction between a plant and a person, but it does not explain how interactions between living things bring good or harm in the ecosystem sense required by the competency.

copy.en:
Is bougainvillea poisonous to touch?

No! The bougainvillea plant itself is not poisonous. Just be careful of its sharp thorns, which can scratch your skin.
copy.tl:
Nakakalason ba ang bougainvillea?

Hindi! Hindi nakakalason ang bougainvillea mismo. Ang dapat lang ingatan ay ang matatalim nitong tinik na puwedeng makagasgas sa balat.
copy.bis:
Makahilo ba ang bougainvillea?

Dili! Dili makahilo ang bougainvillea mismo. Ang angay lang bantayan mao ang talinis niining mga tunok nga makagisi sa panit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: too much water gives bougainvillea more leaves but fewer colorful bracts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water, but it does not teach that water is a basic need of living things. It presents a specific horticultural fact about bougainvillea flowering, which is not directly supporting the competency of identifying basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter.

copy.en:
Does more water mean more bougainvillea flowers?

Nope — too much water gives bougainvillea more leaves but fewer colorful bracts! It actually needs some heat and dryness to bloom a lot.
copy.tl:
Mas maraming tubig, mas maraming bulaklak ng bougainvillea?

Hindi pala — kapag sobra ang tubig, mas maraming dahon pero kaunti ang makukulay na bracts ng bougainvillea! Kailangan pala nito ng kaunting init at tuyo para mamulaklak nang marami.
copy.bis:
Mas daghan tubig, mas daghan bulak sa bougainvillea?

Dili diay — kung sobra ang tubig, mas daghan og dahon apan gamay ra ang kolorado nga bracts sa bougainvillea! Kinahanglan diay kini og gamay nga init ug pagkauga aron mamukad og daghan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The central nervous system includes the brain and spinal cord
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the central nervous system, which is unrelated to weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, humidity, rain, or cloud cover.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The central nervous system includes the brain and spinal cord
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the brain and spinal cord, not about observing or recording weather changes or weather patterns.

copy.en: The central nervous system includes the brain and spinal cord, which act as the main control center of the body.
copy.tl: Ang central nervous system ay binubuo ng utak at spinal cord, na nagsisilbing pangunahing control center ng katawan.
copy.bis: Ang central nervous system gilangkoban sa utok ug spinal cord, nga nagsilbing pangunang control center sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Eating nutritious food, drinking enough water, and exercising regularly all help keep your brain healthy and working well.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses food and water as part of healthy habits for the brain, but does not teach the general basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not identify or describe these needs as a concept; it only mentions two of them in a specific health context.

copy.en: Eating nutritious food, drinking enough water, and exercising regularly all help keep your brain healthy and working well.
copy.tl: Ang masustansyang pagkain, sapat na tubig, at regular na ehersisyo ay tumutulong para manatiling malusog at maayos gumana ang utak.
copy.bis: Ang masustansyang pagkaon, igong tubig, ug regular nga ehersisyo makatabang aron magpabiling himsog ug molihok og maayo ang utok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so it needs constant food and blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food as a need for the brain, but the competency is about identifying the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). The card does not teach this general concept; it only states a specific fact about the brain's energy use and its need for food and blood. This is not direct instructional support for identifying basic needs of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your brain uses about one-fifth (20%) of your whole body's energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems work. The card mentions the brain needing blood, which touches on the circulatory system, but it does not describe how any body system works. It is a trivia fact about brain energy consumption, not an explanation of system function. No direct support.

copy.en: Even though it's small, your brain uses about one-fifth (20%) of your whole body's energy — so it needs constant food and blood!
copy.tl: Kahit maliit lang ang utak, gumagamit ito ng halos ikalimang bahagi (20%) ng enerhiya ng buong katawan — kaya kailangan nito ng tuloy-tuloy na pagkain at dugo!
copy.bis: Bisan gamay ra ang utok, mogamit kini og halos ikalima nga bahin (20%) sa kusog sa tibuok lawas — mao nga nagkinahanglan kini og kanunay nga pagkaon ug dugo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies brass as an alloy of copper and zinc and mentions its golden color and use. It does not investigate properties such as melting point, hardness, or electrical/thermal conductivity, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions copper and zinc and a use of brass, but it does not identify properties and uses of metals such as iron, gold, silver, and copper used by the local community. The content is only loosely related to metals.

copy.en:
Why does brass look so golden?

Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc. It has a beautiful golden-yellow color, perfect for trumpets and shiny decorations!
copy.tl:
Bakit gintong-dilaw ang kulay ng brass?

Ang brass ay isang alloy na gawa sa tanso at zinc. May kulay itong gintong-dilaw, kaya ginagamit ito sa trumpeta at mga dekorasyon!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga bulawan-dalag ang kolor sa brass?

Ang brass usa ka alloy sa tanso ug zinc. Adunay bulawan-dalag nga kolor, busa gigamit kini sa trumpeta ug mga dekorasyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whipping traps tiny air bubbles in the stretchy protein, creating a light, puffy foam.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air bubbles trapped in a foam, but it does not identify or describe the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or classify the foam's components by state. It is only tangentially related to states of matter.

copy.en: Brazo de Mercedes uses beaten egg whites! Whipping traps tiny air bubbles in the stretchy protein, creating a light, puffy foam.
copy.tl: Ang brazo de mercedes ay gawa sa pinalong puti ng itlog! Habang binabati, nahuhuli ng tela-telang protina ang maliliit na bula ng hangin kaya lumalambot at lumalaki.
copy.bis: Ang brazo de mercedes hinimo sa gibatil nga puti sa itlog! Samtang gibatil, madakpan sa unat-unat nga protina ang gagmayng bula sa hangin, mao nga mahimong gaan ug burot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bread mold is very distantly related to humans because its amino acid sequence differs from humans by 48 amino acids.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy

copy.en: Bread mold is very distantly related to humans because its amino acid sequence differs from humans by 48 amino acids.
copy.tl: Ang bread mold ay napakalayo ang kaugnayan sa tao dahil ang amino acid sequence nito ay nagkakaiba ng 48 amino acids mula sa tao.
copy.bis: Ang bread mold layo kaayo ang kalambigitan sa tawo tungod kay ang amino acid sequence niini nagkalahi ug 48 ka amino acids sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The breadfruit, or rimas, is a large starchy fruit from a tree.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a fruit from a tree but does not mention leaves, roots, stems, or their roles in water and nutrient uptake. It does not support the competency's focus on outer plant parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The breadfruit, or rimas, is a large starchy fruit from a tree.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a fact about breadfruit as a food source but does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. No interdependence or environmental dependence is discussed.

copy.en: The breadfruit, or rimas, is a large starchy fruit from a tree. It's cooked before eating, like a vegetable or root crop.
copy.tl: Ang rimas o breadfruit ay isang malaking bunga ng puno na puno ng almirol. Niluluto ito bago kainin, parang gulay o kamoteng-kahoy.
copy.bis: Ang rimas o breadfruit usa ka dako nga bunga sa kahoy nga puno sa almidor. Giluto kini una kan-on, sama sa utanon o lagutmon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Experts recommend babies drink only breastmilk for the first six months, since it's the most complete food for them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses exclusive breastfeeding as complete food for infants, which touches on food as a need but does not teach the general concept of basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). It is a specific nutrition recommendation, not an identification of basic needs.

copy.en: Experts recommend babies drink only breastmilk for the first six months, since it's the most complete food for them.
copy.tl: Inirerekomenda ng mga eksperto na sa unang anim na buwan, gatas lang ng ina ang ibigay sa sanggol dahil ito ang pinakakumpletong pagkain nito.
copy.bis: Girekomendar sa mga eksperto nga sa unang unom ka bulan, gatas lang sa inahan ang ihatag sa masuso kay mao kini ang labing kompleto nga pagkaon niini.

copy.en:
Why did ancient Romans use stone for bridge arches?

Stone is super strong in compression — it doesn't crack easily when squeezed tight!
copy.tl:
Bakit ginamit ng mga sinaunang Roman ang bato sa mga arko ng tulay?

Napaka-lakas ng bato sa compression — hindi ito madaling mabiyak kahit pigain nang malakas!
copy.bis:
Nganong gigamit sa karaang Romano ang bato sa mga arko sa tulay?

Labing lig-on ang bato sa compression — dili kini dali mabuto bisan pindoton og hugot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each cable pulls tight and carries part of the deck's weight up to the tower

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a static bridge where cables exert tension and support the deck, but it never identifies the situation as balanced or unbalanced forces, nor does it contrast the two types as required by the competency. It only mentions forces in a general way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each cable pulls tight and carries part of the deck's weight up to the tower
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies forces (tension and weight) act between objects, but it does not state that forces can be measured or provide any measurement context. It is background knowledge about forces, not direct instruction on identifying that forces act between objects and can be measured.

copy.en: A cable-stayed bridge has cables stretching straight from a tall tower down to the deck — each cable pulls tight and carries part of the deck's weight up to the tower!
copy.tl: Ang cable-stayed bridge ay may mga cable na nakakabit direkta mula sa mataas na tore papuntang deck — bawat cable ay naka-tension at nagdadala ng bahagi ng bigat ng deck pataas sa tore!
copy.bis: Ang cable-stayed bridge adunay mga cable nga direkta gikan sa taas nga tore paingon sa deck — ang matag cable naa sa tension ug nagdala sa bahin sa gibug-aton sa deck paingon sa tore!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The I-beam shape is smart: most material sits at the top and bottom flanges where bending stress is biggest, while the thin web saves weight!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses bending stress and material distribution in an I-beam, but does not describe how forces change the shape of objects (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). It is about structural efficiency, not the effect of forces on shape.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The I-beam shape is smart: most material sits at the top and bottom flanges where bending stress is biggest, while the thin web saves weight!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shape and weight, but does not explore or describe things that affect the movement of objects. It is about static structural design, not movement or factors affecting motion.

copy.en: The I-beam shape is smart: most material sits at the top and bottom flanges where bending stress is biggest, while the thin web saves weight!
copy.tl: Matalino ang hugis I-beam: karamihan ng materyal nasa itaas at ibabang flanges kung saan pinakamalaki ang bending stress, at ang manipis na web ay nagtitipid ng timbang!
copy.bis: Maalamon ang hugis I-beam: kadaghanan sa materyal naa sa ibabaw ug ubos nga flanges diin labing dako ang bending stress, samtang ang manipis nga web nagtipig sa gibug-aton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sirius is the brightest star we can see in the night sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about a specific star (Sirius) but does not support the competency's focus on participating in guided activities to observe and describe natural sky objects. It provides no observational or descriptive activity and only mentions a star without connecting to the broader set of daytime/nighttime objects.

copy.en: Sirius is the brightest star we can see in the night sky!
copy.tl: Ang Sirius ang pinakamaliwanag na bituin na nakikita sa gabing kalangitan!
copy.bis: Ang Sirius mao ang pinakahayag nga bituon nga makita sa kagabhion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It depends on their size, heat, and distance!

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why stars vary in brightness (size, heat, distance). Stars are celestial objects but the competency focuses on the solar system's structure, which this card does not address.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do some stars look dim while others look super bright?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses stars, which are among the natural objects in the sky, but it does not involve guided activities to observe and describe the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. It only explains brightness variation, not observation or description of these objects.

copy.en:
Why do some stars look dim while others look super bright?

It depends on their size, heat, and distance! That's why some near stars look dim, and some far ones look very bright.
copy.tl:
Bakit may malabong bituin at may napakaliwanag ding bituin?

Nakadepende ito sa laki, init, at layo nila! Kaya may malalapit na malabo, at may malalayong napakaliwanag.
copy.bis:
Nganong naay hanap nga bituon ug naay hayag kaayo?

Nagdepende kini sa gidak-on, init, ug kalayo nila! Busa naay duol nga hanap ug halayo nga hayag kaayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keep copies of IDs and a small radio in your go-bag!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a general go-bag packing tip for evacuation, but does not mention PHIVOLCS alert levels or interpreting them. It is only tangentially related to safety before an eruption, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
What important items should you pack in your go-bag before evacuating?

Keep copies of IDs and a small radio in your go-bag! This way, your family can still be identified and informed during and after the eruption.
copy.tl:
Anong mahahalagang gamit ang dapat ilagay sa go-bag bago mag-evacuate?

Magdala ng kopya ng IDs at maliit na radyo sa go-bag! Para makilala at ma-inform pa rin ang pamilya habang nag-e-evacuate at pagkatapos ng pagsabog.

Unsa nga importante nga butang ang butang sa go-bag sa dili pa mag-evacuate?

Pagdala og kopya sa IDs ug gamay nga radyo sa go-bag! Aron mailhan ug ma-inform gihapon ang pamilya panahon sa evacuation ug human sa pagsabog.

Why did people use bronze before iron?

Long ago, people made tools from bronze (copper mixed with tin) before iron, because bronze needs less heat to shape!
copy.tl:
Bakit bronze ang ginamit ng mga tao bago ang bakal?

Noong unang panahon, gumawa muna ang mga tao ng kasangkapan mula sa bronze (tanso na may halong lata) bago ang bakal, dahil mas kaunting init lang ang kailangan para hubugin ito!
copy.bis:
Nganong bronze ang gigamit sa mga tawo sa wala pa ang puthaw?

Kaniadto, naghimo muna ang mga tawo og himan gikan sa bronze (tumbaga nga gisagolan og lata) sa wala pa ang puthaw, kay mas ubos nga init ang gikinahanglan aron hulmahon kini!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper

copy.en:
What metals are mixed together to make the awesome alloy called bronze?

Bronze is a special alloy made by mixing copper with a metal called tin!
copy.tl:
Anong mga metal ang pinaghahalo para makagawa ng napakagandang aleasyon na bronse?

Ang bronse ay isang espesyal na aleasyon na gawa sa paghahalo ng tanso at tin!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga metal ang gisagol aron mahimo ang nindot nga aleasyon nga bronse?

Ang bronse usa ka espesyal nga aleasyon nga gihimo sa pagsagol sa tumbaga ug tin!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper

copy.en:
Why did people in ancient times use bronze to make their weapons and tools?

Because bronze is harder than pure copper, making it perfect for tough ancient tools and weapons!
copy.tl:
Bakit ginamit ng mga tao noon ang bronse para sa kanilang mga sandata at kasangkapan?

Dahil mas matigas ang bronse kaysa sa purong tanso, kaya maganda ito para sa matitibay na sandata at kasangkapan!
copy.bis:
Nganong gigamit sa mga tawo kaniadto ang bronse para sa ilang mga hinagiban ug galamiton?

Tungod kay mas gahi ang bronse kaysa lunsay nga tumbaga, mao nga nindot kini para sa lig-on nga hinagiban!

copy.en:
What is budding in living things?

A tiny outgrowth forms on a parent like yeast or hydra — and over time, it grows into a whole new individual!
copy.tl:
Ano ang budding sa mga buhay na bagay?

May maliit na usbong na tumutubo sa magulang tulad ng yeast o hydra — at unti-unti, ito ay nagiging isang bagong indibidwal!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang budding sa mga buhing butang?

Adunay gamay nga usbong nga motubo sa ginikanan sama sa yeast o hydra — ug sa gidugayon, mahimo kining bag-ong indibidwal!

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant bulb structure and food storage, not about the parts, functions, handling, or storing of a compound microscope.

copy.en: A bulb is a short stem surrounded by fleshy leaves that store food, helping the plant survive dormancy, a resting period, and grow again later.
copy.tl: Ang bulb ay isang maikling stem na napapalibutan ng malalamang mga dahon na nag-iimbak ng pagkain, na tumutulong sa halaman na mabuhay sa dormancy, o panahon ng pahinga, at tumubo muli sa susunod.

copy.en:
Is a Taal alert the same as a Mayon alert?

No! Each PHIVOLCS bulletin names the specific volcano and alert level. Always read the name carefully before you act!
copy.tl:
Ang Taal alert ba ay pareho sa Mayon alert?

Hindi! Bawat PHIVOLCS bulletin ay nagbibigay ng pangalan ng bulkan at alert level. Basahin muna ang pangalan bago kumilos!
copy.bis:
Ang Taal alert ba parehas sa Mayon alert?

Dili! Matag PHIVOLCS bulletin naghatag og ngalan sa bulkan ug alert level. Basaha una ang ngalan bago buhat!

copy.en: Bulusan is an active volcano in Sorsogon, Bicol that often puffs out ash and steam! It sits beside the beautiful Bulusan Lake and is watched by PHIVOLCS for its frequent phreatic activity.
copy.tl: Ang Bulusan ay isang aktibong bulkan sa Sorsogon, Bicol na madalas nagpapalabas ng abo at singaw! Nasa tabi ito ng magandang Bulusan Lake at bantayan ng PHIVOLCS dahil sa madalas na phreatic na aktibidad.
copy.bis: Ang Bulusan usa ka aktibong bulkan sa Sorsogon, Bicol nga kanunay nagpagawas og abo ug singaw! Anaa kini sa kilid sa matahum nga Bulusan Lake ug gibantayan sa PHIVOLCS tungod sa kanunay nga phreatic nga aktibidad.

copy.bis: Nagalutaw ang bangkang Pinoy tungod sa bakante niini nga lawas! Ang mga katig usab ang motabang aron dili kini matakilid.

copy.tl: Kapag namatay ang isda, nagtitipon ang gases mula sa decomposition sa loob nito! Binabawasan nito ang average density ng isda, kaya lumulutang ito sa ibabaw.
copy.bis: Kung mamatay ang isda, magtipon ang gases gikan sa decomposition sulod niini! Kini nagpaubos sa average density sa isda, hinungdan nga mulutaw kini sa ibabaw.

copy.en: Archimedes discovered that the buoyant force pushing an object up equals the exact weight of the water it pushes out of the way!
copy.tl: Natuklasan ni Archimedes na ang puwersang pampalutang sa isang bagay ay katumbas ng timbang ng tubig na natabig o naitulak nito palabas!
copy.bis: Nadiskobrehan ni Archimedes nga ang puwersa nga nagpalutaw sa butang katumbas sa gibug-aton sa tubig nga gitulod niini pagawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the buoyant force pushes up on it

What are burnay jars used for?

In Vigan, Ilocos Sur, people make burnay! These ceramic jars are used to store yummy vinegar and fish paste.

Para saan ang mga burnay na banga?

Sa Vigan, Ilocos Sur, gumagawa ng burnay! Ito ay mga seramikang banga na ginagamit pang-imbak ng suka at bagoong.
copy.bis:
Unsay gamit sa mga burnay nga banga?

Sa Vigan, Ilocos Sur, naghimo silag burnay! Kini mga seramikang banga nga gigamit sa pagtipig og suka ug bagoong.

What gas is released when wood burns?

When wood or charcoal burns, it releases carbon dioxide gas right into the air around us!

Anong gas ang nilalabas kapag nasusunog ang kahoy?

Kapag nasusunog ang kahoy o uling, naglalabas ito ng carbon dioxide gas sa hangin na ating nilalanghap!
copy.bis:
Unsang gas ang mogawas kung masunog ang kahoy?

Kung masunog ang kahoy o uling, mogawas kini og carbon dioxide nga gas sa hangin nga atong ginasinaylan!

Why does fire need air to keep burning?

Anything that burns needs oxygen from the air to keep the flame going!

Bakit kailangan ng apoy ang hangin para tuloy-tuloy ang pagliyab?

Ang anumang nasusunog ay nangangailangan ng oksiheno mula sa hangin para mag-apoy!

Ngano kinahanglan sa kalayo ang hangin aron magpadayon ang pagdilaab?

Ang bisan unsa nga masunog nagkinahanglan og oksiheno gikan sa hangin aron magpadayon ang kalayo!
